Explicit PFP name mappings take precedence over reverse-ordered legacy scanning, cache their first resolution, and do not themselves verify constructor mathematics or authority. Legacy scanning suppresses any ImportError, including an internal dependency failure, so absent and broken optional modules can be conflated. The pure/zero-framework-dependency docstring is an architectural claim, not enforced here. Import-based probes must account for transitive exception initialization and lazy target modules; no package execution occurred.

Read all shared-kernel names and exact lazy mappings. TYPE_CHECKING declarations are inert at runtime; __getattr__ imports only the registered target, caches it, and propagates its errors. __dir__ exposes the declared public set. Aliases distinguish shared WireKey from key.WireKeyVO and centralize authority, budget, exact/canonical and result primitives. This module supplies no validation beyond routing; guarantees depend on the selected owners, not the names.

Read singleton enum and validator. The accepted representation is the rendered string None: enum values are unwrapped, all other objects pass through str. Consequently Python None and any object rendering None also pass despite the annotated str-or-enum boundary. This is representation permissiveness rather than demonstrated authorization gain; caller behavior needs inspection. No capability or execution isolation is implemented by this label validator.

Read immutable nominal budget classes, all limits and capacity check. Constructors reject booleans and out-of-range values, with class-sensitive equality/hash; from_int is stricter than constructors about integer subclasses. Candidate capacity refuses count>=budget but assumes a valid nonnegative integer count and consumes no resource itself. Operation/step/execution/time are positive bounded data, not clocks or enforced execution meters. Downstream callers must bind and decrement them consistently.

Read complete Fraction conversion and canonical parser. Floats/booleans are rejected; integer/Fraction inputs stay exact. Round-trip rendering rejects whitespace, leading zeros, nonreduced fractions, signed denominator variants and alternate spellings after int parsing, so wire equality tracks normalized rational equality. Residual zero is exact only for correctly sourced rational inputs, not a validation of upstream modeling. The docstring rationale that decimal or exponent strings are not exactly representable is mathematically wrong: finite decimal strings denote exact rationals; refusal is a chosen wire grammar. No magnitude/string-length budget is imposed here beyond interpreter integer limits. Stdlib-only module is read-vetted for future isolated tests.

Read Success/Failure dataclasses, mapping/binding/error mapping and factories. Failure short-circuits functions and unsafe unwrap raises; Success delegates callbacks directly. Monad-style composition relies on callbacks returning the declared Result type and does not catch exceptions or validate payloads. Frozen wrappers do not recursively freeze arbitrary contained data. AuthorityEffect None is a docstring rather than enforcement; these are generic control-flow containers, not acceptance certificates. Stdlib-only module is read-vetted for isolated tests.

Read rational interval arithmetic, root isolation, algebraic comparison/sign and limits. Closed interval products take four extrema; Alg uses monic squarefree polynomial and one-root half-open interval. Mathematical equality is alg_equal via gcd/intersection, while __eq__ compares presentation fields. isolate squarefrees first and recursively bisects without a global operation budget; comparison/sign have4096 refinement caps. Constructor accepts a mutable list despite tuple annotation and leaves it attached: probe changes polynomial from x-1 to x-2 and changes represented value after construction. Input endpoints/coefficient types rely mostly on downstream operations. General root_count endpoint defect does not automatically invalidate squarefree isolate/Alg construction paths.

Read all rational polynomial operations, Euclidean division/gcd, squarefree reduction, Sturm variations and bound. Arithmetic is low-to-high coefficients with trim and no coefficient/size validation beyond Q operations. root_count claims distinct roots for arbitrary polynomials but feeds the unreduced polynomial to a Sturm chain and simply removes zero signs at endpoints. For(x-1)^2(x-2), this returns0 on(1,3] instead of1 and2 on(0,1] instead of1; ordinary nonroot endpoints(0,3] returns2. Squarefree reduction or suitable endpoint handling is needed for this public contract. Cauchy bound is conservatively max coefficient magnitude+2.

Read shape checking and all injected linear-algebra calls. as_matrix requires Q entries and rectangular rows; square/symmetry checks precede determinant, characteristic polynomial and positivity interfaces. Algorithms and returned values are trusted from one mutable process-global port; no runtime port conformance, returned rank range, minor count, rational result or positivity proof is checked. first_nonpositive_minor accepts an empty returned minor sequence as success. Sylvester criterion is valid for real symmetric matrices when all leading minors are correctly computed; this facade does not certify its injected implementation. Unbound port explicitly refuses.
